newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOREIGN BUYING OF DANISH MORTGAGE BONDS UP - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN BUYING OF DANISH MORTGAGE BONDS UP - REPORT.

text.p: Foreign investors' interest in buying Danish mortgage bonds has risen markedly in the past few years, a Copenhagen Stock Exchange report said on Tuesday.

The report showed that five percent of all Danish mortgage credit bonds, at a nominal value of almost 50 billion crowns, are in foreign investors' hands compared with less than two per cent or only around 15 billion crowns four years ago.
Foreign investors hold 35 percent of the total 670 billion crowns of Danish state bonds in circulation, it said.
The report, written by a Danish Mortgage Credit Council consultant, said that a total foreign holding of 10-15 percent in the foreseeable future, would be desirable.
It said that Danish mortgage credit paper would never achieve the same popularity with overseas investors as state bonds.
